- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some of the most popular hiking trails in Banff National Park are: 
  1. Plain of Six Glaciers - Moderate hike
  2. Lake Agnes Tea House - Moderate hike
  3. Sentinel Pass - Difficult hike
  4. Johnston Canyon - Easy hike
  5. Cascade Mountain - Difficult hike
  6. Sulphur Mountain - Moderate hike
  7. Sunshine Meadows - Easy to moderate hike
  8. Larch Valley - Moderate hike
  9. Consolation Lakes - Moderate hike
  10. Banff Legacy Trail - Easy bike/walking trail
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The difficulty level of each hike may vary based on individual fitness level and hiking experience. It is recommended to check trail conditions, weather forecast, and carry adequate supplies before starting any hike.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested camping spots near hiking trails in Banff National Park:
  1. Two Jack Lakeside Campground - Near Lake Minnewanka and Cascade Mountain
  2. Tunnel Mountain Campground - Near Banff Legacy Trail, Sulphur Mountain, and Sentinel Pass
  3. Johnston Canyon Campground - Near Johnston Canyon
  4. Lake Louise Campground - Near Plain of Six Glaciers and Lake Agnes Tea House
  5. Two Medicine Lake Campground - Near Consolation Lakes
  6. Castle Mountain Campground - Near Larch Valley
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These campgrounds fill up quickly during peak season, so it's recommended to make reservations in advance. There are also backcountry camping options available for some of these trails.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It might be better to focus on a few trails and campgrounds at a time, especially if this is the user's first time visiting Banff National Park.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested popular and stunning viewpoints in Banff National Park:
  1. Lake Louise
  2. Moraine Lake
  3. Sulphur Mountain
  4. Johnston Canyon
  5. Vermilion Lakes
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These viewpoints are popular and typically crowded, so it's best to visit early in the morning or late in the evening to avoid crowds.
